Sleep
Although sufﬁcient sleep is vital for normal growth and cognitive development in childhood and adolescence, short sleep duration
can also impact on nutritional intake and obesity risk. Studies in adolescents and young adults have found associations between
a lack of nightime sleep and increases in BMI. Short sleep duration could inﬂuence body weight by disrupting appetite control,
reducing physical activity levels (e.g., due to tiredness), or affecting thermoregulation.
